blocks.etymology: From Middle English humour, from Old French humor, humour, from Latin hūmor, correctly ūmor (“liquid”), from hūmeō, correctly ūmeō (“to be moist”). The h in these words, which was silent in late Classical Latin, is folk etymological, due to the erroneous association with the word humus (“soil”). The shift in meaning "liquid" > "mood" is attributed to the classical system of physiology, where human behaviour is regulated by four bodily humours (fluids). The sense "mood" gave rise to the verb sense "to give in to someone's mood or whim" and, by narrowing of meaning, the sense "wit".

blocks.etymology: Inherited from Middle English whitenesse, whitnesse, whytnesse, hwitnesse, from Old English hwītnes (“whiteness”), equivalent to white + -ness.

senses.definition: the quality or state of being white in appearance

examples.en: She was amazed by the brilliant whiteness of the fresh snow.
examples.vi: Cô ấy kinh ngạc trước sắc trắng rực rỡ của tuyết mới rơi.

senses.definition: the social status, identity, or cultural experience associated with being white

examples.en: The course explores the history of race and ideas of whiteness.
examples.vi: Khóa học khám phá lịch sử chủng tộc và các quan niệm về bản sắc da trắng.

senses.vi: đặc tính da trắng; bản sắc da trắng

thesaurus.definition: the quality or state of the achromatic color of greatest lightness (bearing the least resemblance to black)
the state of being unsullied by sin or moral wrong; lacking a knowledge of evil
lightness or fairness of complexion

vi_block: Sự ngây th, sự trong trắng.

wiktionary.gloss: The state or quality of being white (all senses).
The quality of being white (in the racial sense).
The quality of being white noise.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English wildernes, wildernesse (“desolate or uninhabited place, desolation”) [and other forms], and then either: * from Middle English wilderne (“deserted or uninhabited place, wilderness; land not yet settled”) [and other forms] (from Old English wilddeōren (“savage, wild”); see below) + -nes, -nesse (suffix forming abstract nouns denoting qualities or states); or

senses.definition: A large area of land that has not been cultivated or built on by humans.

examples.en: They spent a week hiking through the wilderness.
examples.vi: Họ đã dành một tuần đi bộ xuyên qua vùng hoang dã.

senses.vi: vùng hoang vu; vùng hoang dã

senses.definition: A period when a politician or group has lost power, office, or public support.

examples.en: He returned after ten years in the political wilderness.
examples.vi: Ông trở lại sau mười năm vắng bóng trên chính trường.

senses.vi: thời kỳ mất quyền lực; nơi vắng vẻ tiêu điều

thesaurus.definition: (politics) a state of disfavor
a wild and uninhabited area left in its natural condition
a bewildering profusion

vi_block: Vùng hoang vu, vùng hoang dã.
Nơi vắng vẻ tiêu điều, nơi hoang tàn.

wiktionary.gloss: Uncultivated and unsettled land in its natural state inhabited by wild animals and with vegetation growing wild; (countable) a tract of such land; a waste or wild.
A place other than land (for example, the air or sea) that is uncared for, and therefore devoted to disorder or wildness.
An ornamental part of a garden or park cultivated with trees and often a maze to evoke a natural wilderness.
Chiefly followed by of: a bewildering flock or throng; a large, often jumbled, collection of things.
A place or situation that is bewildering and in which one may get lost.
Preceded by in the: a situation of disfavour or lack of recognition; (specifically, politics) of a politician, political party, etc.: a situation of being out of office.
